column1: # Generated by scripts/corpus/merge-forms.ts — one row per pair of cards that are forms of
# each other, merged or kept, with the reason. The authority is FORM_RULINGS in
# form-rulings.ts; this file is the readable record of what it did.

column7: why

die Daten is the plural of das Datum, and it is the one row here where the sense really does shift with number — so the gloss says both and the learner meets them on one card. The definition does **not** move: "Facts and figures collected for study or reference" defines the plural and would read as the definition of *das Datum*. The keeper is left with none, for the definition programme (BACKLOG Now #5).

die Medien is the press and broadcasting — a B1 word in its own right — while das Medium at C1 is a medium in the technical or spiritualist sense. Same relationship as Schuld/Schulden, and the four-level gap is the evidence.

Not one word twice: a nominalised adjective whose article names the referent. The cards gloss themselves "acquaintance (male)" and "acquaintance (female)" and their examples follow — the same pair as der Lehrer / die Lehrerin, which BACKLOG wants more of, not fewer.

One word, and gender-audit already ruled der/das both correct (Duden: "der, auch das"). That ruling was about the gender *field* of one card and did not notice there were two, at the same level, with an identical gloss and an identical definition.

die Handschuhe is the plural of der Handschuh. The A2 copy sits in *Skiing and snowboarding*, which is the sector disagreement corpus:dupes flagged for this word in 2026-08-11; the A1 card is in *Clothing* and stays there.

One word. der Joghurt is the standard German form and das Joghurt the Austrian and Swiss one; Duden lists both under a single entry. The two cards carry the same gloss, the same definition and the same plural, so this is a duplicate that survived corpus:dupes only because the article is part of the term.
die Muskeln is the plural of der Muskel. Same level, so the singular simply absorbs it.
die Schuhe is the plural of der Schuh, which the A1 card already records.

der Stiefel has an invariant plural — die Stiefel — so the two headwords are the same string and differ only by article. Not a gender variant: die is the plural article and the card glosses itself "boots".
die Alpen is a proper name. die Alp is an alpine pasture (and, separately, a nightmare); the mountain range is not its plural in any useful sense.
das Angeln is angling, the nominalised infinitive of angeln; die Angeln would be fishing rods. Neuter, again.
die Emissionen is the plural of die Emission (the keeper writes it "-en").

column6: keeper relevelled B1→A2; retired sector University & study
column7: die Kenntnisse is the plural of die Kenntnis. The only row here whose keeper sits *above* the card being retired, so the keeper moves down to A2 — merging upward would take the word off an A2 learner who has it today, which is the reason relevel-a1.ts demotes nothing. The definition moves in the other direction: the retired card says "The things a person knows about a subject." where the keeper says "knowledge; science (knowledge gained through study or practice)", which is the enumeration class BACKLOG Now #5 exists to remove. Retiring the card would have thrown away the better one.

die Nudeln is the plural of die Nudel; the B1 card also carried four synonyms for the *verb* nudeln (herunternudeln, durchnudeln, ableiern, ausnudeln), which is a separate word — they are dropped rather than unioned onto a noun.
das Reisen is the nominalised infinitive — travelling, the activity — not the plural of die Reise (a trip). Neuter, as every nominalised infinitive is.
die Sandalen is the plural of die Sandale.

die Schulden (debts) and die Schuld (guilt, fault) have parted company in meaning. German uses the plural for the money sense and the singular for the moral one; teaching them as one card would teach neither.
die Socken is the plural of die Socke. Both cards say so in their own plural field.
der Westen is the compass point; die Weste is a waistcoat. Unrelated words that collide only because Weste happens to pluralise to Westen.

The plural of the phrase, filed without an article and with pos=noun/gender=null. Its definition ("Energy from sources that do not run out, like sun and wind.") is a definition of the lemma, not of the plural, so it moves.
